page.layout: One page of text. Above the text: two round portrait medallions side by side (no text block of their own, legends only). Below them: the main text in one full-width column. Running head at top centre. Page number top right.

main_text.p: ABRAHAM filius Thare, Deo fuit charissimus, cuius iussu paretem, patriam, omnésque reliquit cognatos: & assumpto Lot abiit in Chanaan peregrinatum, anno mundi 2024. ante Christum natum 1938. promisit illi Deus se in semine illius benedicturu omnes gentes: de semine siquidé huius nascituru erat Christus. huic promissioni adiecta est circuncisio: itaque se & suos circuncidit, annos natus 99. haec circuncisio indicabat vitam æternā habituros, piè in Deum per Christum credentes. Anno ætatis 86. ex ancilla Agar genuit Ismaël, quam illi permisit vxor Sara, cum hæc minimè pareret. At verò nihilominus annos ipse natus centum, & Sara nonaginta, genuerunt, fauore diuino, ipsum Isaac. Abraham obiit diem suum annos natus 175. sepelierunt eum filij sui in Hebron cum Sara, quæ illic sepulta erat, iam ante annos 38. Vide Gene. 11. cap. vsq; ad 25. item Iose. lib. Anti. 1. à cap. 16. vsque ad 26. Post mortem vxoris Sarę, Abraham aliam duxit vxorem, nomine Ceturam, ex qua filios sustulit sex.

SARA, filia Aran, vxor Abraham, proba atque insignis matrona extitit, pulchra quidem ac viro charissima, patientissima & prudentissima mulier. Hæc vti dictum est, annos nata 90. non sine miraculo, Isaac peperit, cùm antea sterilis esset. annos nata 127. moritur. Vide Gene. 23. cap.

page.notes: Two round medallion portraits at top: left labelled "ABRAM FIL. THARE" (Abraham), right labelled "SARRA VX. ABRA." (Sara). No marginal notes. Printed text is in roman with a few words in italic-like spacing; I have written it in roman. The word "sustulit" and "paretem" are as printed. The "s" forms in "sustulit" and "esset" are long s rendered as s in the scan; per the rules these should be plain s, so the transcription uses s. Words "vti", "nata" and "Anti." are as printed; the scan is slightly blurred around "Christum natum" and "ancilla Agar" but these read clearly.
